script: The 50/30/20 rule is everywhere. Fifty percent needs, thirty percent wants, twenty percent savings. Sounds perfect. But if you make less than three thousand a month, it quietly falls apart. Here's why. At low income, needs alone eat past seventy percent of your paycheck. Rent. Food. Gas. There's no thirty percent left for wants, let alone twenty for savings. So what actually works? Flip the math. Try seventy-twenty-ten. Seventy for needs, twenty for wants, ten for savings, even five dollars a week counts. But here's the part nobody mentions. The habit matters more than the percentage. A five dollar deposit every Friday builds the muscle that a broken 50/30/20 rule never will. The real rule isn't fifty-thirty-twenty. It's whatever percentage you'll actually keep.
